title: PACE: Post-Causal Entropy Modeling for Learned LiDAR Point Cloud Compression
claim: Prior methods repeat the full context backbone at every causal step; ours runs it once and confines causality to a light, scalable predictor.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, repeated stacked columns versus branching switch
description: Two panels contrast two ways to model octree occupancy. Panel (a), 'Existing fully-causal modeling', shows four identical columns in sequence. Each column stacks an Ancestors/Siblings box, a yellow Causal Backbone box and a gray Predictor box, ending in a row of colored circles. The siblings fill in one at a time, from dotted question-mark circles to colored ones, and arrows step from one column to the next. This repeats the backbone and predictor four times. Panel (b), 'Proposed post-causal PACE', shows one Ancestors box feeding one yellow Non-Causal Backbone. A rotary switch then routes to One-Stage, Two-Stage and n-Stage chains of gray Stage-Scalable Predictor boxes. Each chain outputs colored circles, with dotted placeholders in the intermediate stages. The eye goes first to the repeated yellow backbones on the left, then to the single backbone and branching paths on the right.
caption: Octree-based LPCC paradigm. (a) Conventional fully-causal modeling, which demands repeated backbone and predictor executions due to intra-level causality constraints. (b) Proposed post-causal pipeline, which constrains causality to a lightweight and stage-scalable predictor only, reducing computational overhead and supporting dynamic stage transitions.
abstract: LiDAR point cloud compression is vital for autonomous systems to handle massive data from high-resolution sensors. While learned entropy modeling built upon octree structures yields high compression gains, it faces two critical bottlenecks: 1) prohibitive latency, particularly during decoding, caused by causal, multi-stage context modeling; and 2) a rigid performance-latency trade-off, preventing a single model from adapting to varying constraints. These limitations stem from the tight coupling between the context aggregation backbone and probability prediction. To address this, we propose PACE, a new framework that reformulates ancestral context aggregation as a non-causal backbone and confines causality to a lightweight, stage-scalable predictor, eliminating repetitive backbone executions and reducing computational overhead. The predictor supports an arbitrary number of prediction stages, enabling seamless adaptation across diverse performance-latency trade-offs without reloading parameters. Experiments demonstrate that PACE sets a new state-of-the-art in compression efficiency, achieving notable BD-BR savings and reducing decoding latency by over 90\% in autoregressive mode, making it attractive for practical applications.
